newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks swing in choppy trade, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks swing in choppy trade, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: U.S. blue chips gyrated in early trade Friday, and the Dow's choppy swings caused the New York Stock Exchange to set, lift, then re-impose trading curbs.
"Volatility continues to be the name of the game," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 44 points at 7698. The New York Stock Exchange set curbs on index-arbitrage trade eight minutes after the market opened, when the Dow made a swift move higher.
Curbs were lifted at 1010 EDT/1410 GMT, then re-imposed 10 minutes later as the Dow surged again.
The stock market was growing nervous ahead of next week's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the employment report for June, analysts said.
"The market has a case of pre-FOMC jitters," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "It's taking some bets about what's going to happen next week."
The Nasdaq composite, which ended lower yesterday, was up four points, while the long bond rose 5/32 to a 6.77 percent yield. Recent softness in bonds has spooked stocks.
A strong University of Michigan consumer confidence index reading of 104.5 did not sway stocks much, Froehlich said.
